one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Mumbai Zaveri Bazar based B2B wholesaler of hand-crafted 22-karat and 18-karat gold jewellery, operating an asset-light model in which all production is outsourced to Karigars through Jobworkers.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is engaged in the business of hand-crafted gold jewellery and provides customisation services to its clients, depending on third-party jobworkers for production and manufacturing of products; it does not manufacture any jewellery in-house. It acts as principal contractor, managing design, material sourcing and the finished jewellery making process, and also provides custom job work services where clients supply bullion along with specific design requirements. Customers are corporate jewellery chains (Joyalukkas India Limited, Kalyan Jewellers India Limited, P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited, P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited, Novel Jewels Limited (Aditya Birla Group), D.P Abhushan Limited and others) and non-corporate jewellers, served PAN India from Mumbai, Maharashtra.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light, non-integrated wholesale model with no backward manufacturing integration and no forward retail integration. The Company describes itself as a wholesale (B2B) player in hand-crafted gold jewellery that acts as principal contractor, managing design, material sourcing and the finished jewellery making process for its clients. Under the heading 'Capacity' the RHP states: 'The manufacturing process is predominantly outsourced to skilled job workers, commonly referred to as Karigars... Hence, we don't have any in-house manufacturing capacity.' Backward: the Company procures pure gold (995 or 999 purity) from bullion dealers / gold merchants, all BIS-marked with the refiner's bar number on the bar and on the invoice; raw material purchases by type (as printed, % of Total Purchase) were Gold Bar 93.27% / 87.12% / 85.61%, Gold Ornaments 6.63% / 12.80% / 14.30%, Stones nil / 0.00% / 0.09%, Miscellaneous 0.10% / 0.08% / 0.00% for FY 2026 / FY 2025 / FY 2024, with total raw material cost of Rs. 15,009.92 million, Rs. 13,231.06 million and Rs. 9,928.30 million respectively; the RHP states the Company does not enter into long-term agreements with suppliers. Production: 72 jobworkers were associated during Fiscal 2026 (87 in Fiscal 2025, 90 in Fiscal 2024), of whom 66 have executed the Company's prescribed agreements, giving access to multiple Karigars; jobworker attrition was 17.24% (Fiscal 2026), 3.33% (Fiscal 2025) and 1.10% (Fiscal 2024); major jobworker manufacturing units are located in Mumbai, Maharashtra. In-house functions retained are design (3 designers in each of Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024), inventory management, purity/metal-pin testing, finishing, final quality control, labelling and photography, and app/online listing - a nine-step process ending with mixed inventory held at the office for clients visiting in person. Forward: the Company does not operate retail showrooms; its Corporate and Non-Corporate Clients resell through their own retail showrooms or online channels. Its mobile application on Google Play Store and App Store is used to showcase designs to clients and is expressly not meant for sale of products. Operations are focused exclusively on domestic markets within India, with a customer network spanning 21 states and 4 union territories; customer counts were 418 (Fiscal 2026), 457 (Fiscal 2025) and 448 (Fiscal 2024), split into repeat customers of 334 / 291 / 279 and new customers of 84 / 166 / 169. Inventory intensity: inventory was Rs. 2,399.58 million / Rs. 1,615.84 million / Rs. 1,314.26 million (62.06% / 66.28% / 75.48% of current assets) with inventory days of 54 / 42 / 45 and inventory turnover of 6.80 / 8.69 / 8.08 for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024; working capital facilities were Rs. 1,670.00 million as at March 31, 2026, and the Company intends to utilise Rs. 380.00 million of Net Proceeds towards working capital and Rs. 1,580 million towards repayment of working capital debt. Product returns were Rs. 1,177.56 million / Rs. 733.98 million / Rs. 462.72 million, being 7.22% / 5.23% / 4.36% of revenue from operations for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024, which the RHP attributes primarily to customer preference-related adjustments rather than quality issues. Headcount: 46 permanent employees as of May 31, 2026 (Executive Directors and KMP 4, Accounts and Finance 4, Administration 16, Sales and Marketing 5, Designing and Client Servicing 11, Quality 6), against 44 / 33 / 31 payroll employees at the end of Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 with employee attrition of 10.39% / 6% / 0%. Insurance covering the gold inventory includes a Jewellers Block Protector Policy no. 48057391 from Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Company Limited providing coverage up to Rs. 4,762.50 million, valid to October 28, 2026.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Gold price and raw-material cost is the dominant cost driver - gold bar was 93.27% of total purchases in FY2026 (87.12% FY2025, 85.61% FY2024), with gold ornaments 6.63%; exposure to import duties, global conditions and international supply/demand
- Gross profit margin expanded from 4.27% (FY2024) to 5.56% (FY2025) to 11.06% (FY2026) while quantity of gold processed FELL from 1,795.52 kg (FY2024) and 1,935.92 kg (FY2025) to 1,397.48 kg (FY2026) - i.e. FY2026 revenue growth of 16.17% came with lower physical volume, on a ~44% rise in gold price (CareEdge) and a ~24% CY25 volume decline in industry demand
- Working capital cycle is lengthening - Core NWC days rose from 58.85 (FY2024) to 62.35 (FY2025) to 81.33 (FY2026); working capital funds inventory of raw material and trade receivables for large and growing clients
- Deleveraging is in progress - net debt to equity 1.80 (FY2024) to 1.44 (FY2025) to 0.80 (FY2026); net debt to EBITDA 3.79 to 2.22 to 1.06; Rs 1,580.00 million of Net Proceeds earmarked for repayment of borrowings
- Customer mix shifting toward corporate clients (55.08% of revenue FY2024 to 64.25% FY2026), with top-10 concentration rising to 39.56% in FY2026 from 30.48% (FY2025) and 30.62% (FY2024)
- Ability to expand the design portfolio and to retain existing / attract new customers - total customers 448 (FY2024), 457 (FY2025), 418 (FY2026); repeat customers 279, 291, 334
- Product returns are a recurring drag - Rs 1,177.56 million or 7.22% of total revenue in FY2026, up from Rs 733.98 million (5.23%) FY2025 and Rs 462.72 million (4.36%) FY2024
- Jobworker base is contracting with rising attrition - 90 (FY2024), 87 (FY2025), 72 (FY2026) jobworkers; attrition rate 1.10%, 3.33%, 17.24%
- Consumer spending, seasonality of festivals and the discretionary nature of jewellery purchases drive demand; general economic and market conditions in India and globally

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Capturing market opportunities in the growing jewellery industry - scale operations to handle increased demand as organised retail clients expand, and leverage expertise to secure more business from existing clients
- Leverage operational capacity, supplier relationships and existing client connections; tailor product offerings to market trends and client needs to solidify position as a trusted B2B partner
- Continue to participate in exhibitions to build partnerships, expand the client base and stay updated on industry trends, aiming to increase recurring sales and grow transaction volumes
- Augment fund-based capacities and reduce dependence on debt in order to create long-term shareholder value and be able to scale up business operations - Rs 1,580 million of Offer proceeds earmarked for repayment of working capital debt and Rs 380.00 million for working capital
- Continue to invest in marketing and brand building initiatives - B2B exhibitions and trade shows, social media, regional jewellery magazines, personalised store visits and a design-showcase mobile application

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: There is no plant or manufacturing capacity expansion: the Company runs an asset-light model and 'we don't manufacture any jewellery in-house', with all production outsourced to localised Karigars through Jobworkers. The stated expansion narrative is instead commercial and balance-sheet led - scaling volumes to serve the growth of organised corporate retail clients (Kalyan, Joyalukkas, P N Gadgil, Novel Jewels/Aditya Birla) whose store expansion is expected to drive additional demand for the Company's crafted pieces; deepening penetration of the existing PAN-India client base (21 states and 4 union territories) and adding new clients through IIJS/PMI/GJS exhibitions; and augmenting fund-based capacity by repaying working-capital borrowings and adding incremental working capital from the Fresh Issue so that inventory and receivables can support larger client orders. The Company holds three leased offices in Zaveri Bazar, Mumbai and the RHP discloses no new premises, plant or capacity addition.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong historical financial results - revenue from operations grew from Rs 10,617.83 million (FY2024) to Rs 14,038.26 million (FY2025) to Rs 16,307.87 million (FY2026); EBITDA Rs 285.99 mn to Rs 653.47 mn to Rs 1,579.00 mn; PAT Rs 128.16 mn to Rs 403.12 mn to Rs 1,066.81 mn
- Long term relation with local Jobworkers for handling custom hand-crafted gold jewellery making process - 72 jobworkers engaged in Fiscal 2026, of which 66 have entered into agreements with the Company, giving access to multiple specialised Karigars
- Asset-light business model - no in-house manufacturing infrastructure, letting the Company focus on inventory management, design and customisation
- Wide product range in hand crafted gold jewellery under one roof (22-karat and 18-karat across Antique, Semi-Antique, Calcutta, Temple, Gheru Polish and Yellow/Rhodium/Rose Gold categories)
- Commitment to quality and customer satisfaction - all gold jewellery hallmarked by BIS, quality control team inspects design, craftsmanship, metal purity and stone setting on each piece
- Established relations with corporate and non-corporate jewellery clients - 418 customers in Fiscal 2026 of which 334 repeat customers; corporate clients include Joyalukkas, Kalyan Jewellers, P N Gadgil Jewellers and Novel Jewels (Aditya Birla Group)
- Experienced Promoters and management team with execution capabilities - over three decades in the jewellery industry, business started in 1992
- Established marketing setup - participation in IIJS Signature, IIJS Premiere, IIJS Tritiya, PMI and GJS exhibitions plus a design showcase application

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Total dependence on third-party Jobworkers and Karigars for 100% of production, with a shrinking and increasingly volatile jobworker base — 'We are dependent on third party Jobworkers for the production and manufacturing of all of our products.' Jobworkers fell from 90 (FY2024) to 87 (FY2025) to 72 (FY2026) while attrition rose from 1.10% to 3.33% to 17.24%. Karigars do not work exclusively for the Company, their skills are transmitted informally, and any scarcity of Karigars in Maharashtra would materially affect output. Jobworkers and Karigars also gain access to proprietary designs.
- Working-capital intensity and significant indebtedness in a gold-price-inflated inventory business — Core NWC days rose from 58.85 (FY2024) to 81.33 (FY2026). The Company 'requires significant amounts of working capital for continued growth' and intends to use Rs 380.00 million of Net Proceeds for it, plus Rs 1,580.00 million to repay borrowings. Net debt to equity was still 0.80x at FY2026. Negative net cash flow from operating activities of Rs 231.05 million was reported in Fiscal 2025. The Company has also availed unsecured borrowing repayable on demand and Promoters have given personal guarantees.
- Gold price volatility directly re-values inventory and drives income — 'Volatility in the market price of gold has a bearing on the value of our inventory and could affect our income.' Gold bar was 93.27% of FY2026 purchases; gold price rose ~44% in CY25 while jewellery demand volume fell ~24% (CareEdge - commissioned industry report, not the issuer's own disclosure). Gold processed dropped to 1,397.48 kg in FY2026 from 1,935.92 kg in FY2025, so revenue growth was price-led, not volume-led.
- Customer concentration and reliance on the commercial success of clients' own retail businesses — Top 10 customers were 39.56% of revenue in FY2026, up sharply from 30.48% (FY2025) and 30.62% (FY2024); top 5 were 23.26% and the top 1 customer 6.12%. The Company is a B2B supplier whose demand 'is reliant on the success of our customers' products with end consumers', and it does not maintain a formal order book.
- Geographic concentration of both revenue and of the sourcing/manufacturing ecosystem — Top 5 states (Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha) contributed 67.84% of FY2026 revenue, rising from 62.00% in FY2024. Separately, all operations run out of three leased offices in Zaveri Bazar, Mumbai and Karigar supply is concentrated in Maharashtra, exposing the Company to regional economic, cultural and geopolitical shocks.
- Quality-control failures manifesting as rising customer returns — Products returned by customers amounted to Rs 1,177.56 million (7.22% of total revenue) in FY2026, versus Rs 733.98 million (5.23%) in FY2025 and Rs 462.72 million (4.36%) in FY2024 - a rising trend the Company characterises as not material to results of operations.
- Related-party dependence and promoter control, including occupation of promoter-group premises — Related party transactions were Rs 633.39 million (3.88% of revenue) in FY2026, Rs 694.95 million (4.95%) FY2025 and Rs 958.92 million (9.03%) FY2024, principally remuneration, interest on unsecured loans and rent. Promoters hold 74.25% pre-Offer and will retain majority post-Offer. The Registered and Corporate Office is leased from Promoter Group individual Sushila Kantilal Jain (with Mangala Jugraj Jain).
- Governance / listed-company inexperience and disclosed regulatory non-compliances — 'None of our Directors have prior experience of directorships in listed companies.' The RHP also discloses certain instances of non-compliances and alleged non-compliances with respect to certain regulatory filings. All operations depend heavily on the three Promoters, and the Company has paid no dividends in the last three Fiscals.
